title: Ze’iri (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as a Babylonian and as Rav’s student, taking as proof [Yevamot 21a:18-20](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.21a.18-20): “Rav said: Four women … and Ze’iri adds: also his mother’s father’s wife.” So it is in Yuchasin that Ze’iri learned from Rav; and so it is cited in the [Rosh on Bava Kamma 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Bava_Kamma.3.7), that Rav was Ze’iri’s teacher.[^3]

Ze’iri also speaks in Rav Kahana’s name, as in [Bava Metzia 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.60b.3) and [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.2.22). He went up to the Land of Israel still in Rabbi Chanina’s lifetime, as we find Ze’iri speaking in Rabbi Chanina’s name in [Shabbat 17a:7-8](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.17a.7-8) and [Shabbat 50a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.50a.10), [Ketubot 15a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.15a.3), [Sanhedrin 98a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.98a.7), [Menachot 21a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.21a.5) and [Menachot 30b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.30b.10), and [Niddah 19b:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.19b.17). Likewise we find in the Jerusalem Talmud “Rabbi Ze’ira in the name of Rabbi Chanina,” as in [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.5.2.5), [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 2:2:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.2.2.3) and [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.3.4.4), and Hyman considers him undoubtedly Ze’iri.[^4]

He was a distinguished student of Rabbi Yochanan, as in [Kiddushin 71b:3-4](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.71b.3-4): Ze’iri was avoiding Rabbi Yochanan, for Rabbi Yochanan used to say to him, “Marry my daughter.” One day they were walking on the road and came to a pool of water; he carried Rabbi Yochanan on his shoulder and took him across. He said to him: “Our Torah is fit, and our daughters are not fit?” In [Avodah Zarah 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.53a.7), Ze’iri speaks in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.

In [Yoma 9b:15-18](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.9b.15-18), in one of Rav Papa’s alternatives, Resh Lakish was bathing in the Jordan; Ze’iri came and gave him his hand; he said to him: “By God, I hate you [Babylonians],” etc.

Afterward he went down to Babylonia, and this is what we find in [Chullin 56a:5-6](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.56a.5-6): “When Ze’iri went up (from Babylonia) to Nehardea” (Hyman explains this by saying that their route to the Land of Israel or from the Land of Israel was by way of Sura, which is Babylonia without further designation, and Sura lies below Nehardea, as in Taanit 10b; when Ze’iri came to Babylonia he came to Sura and afterward went up to Nehardea), he said: “But thus they said in Resh Lakish’s name.” There he was a colleague of Rav Nachman, as in [Bava Batra 157a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.157a.11), where Rav Nachman called him “Ze’iri our colleague”; but Hyman considers Ze’iri much older than Rav Nachman and points to [Avodah Zarah 61b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.61b.8), where Rav Nachman speaks in the name of Ze’iri. Rav Huna’s great students spoke in his name, such as Rabbah and Rav Yosef, [Nedarim 46a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.46a.9).[^5]

Likewise we find Abba bar Chanan in his name, [Avodah Zarah 60b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.60b.10); Abba bar Rav Chisda, [Avodah Zarah 49b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.49b.6); Abba bar Chama, [Avodah Zarah 31a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.31a.7); and Surchav bar Pappa in his name, [Ketubot 17b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.17b.2). Rava speaks in the name of Ze’iri in [Sotah 5a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.5a.2), and Rava said of him, [Zevachim 43b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.43b.10): “Every baraita that Ze’iri does not explain is not explained.”

He is mentioned in [Gittin 87b:6-8](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.87b.6-8), “Ze’iri taught,” and in Yoma 27b as cited by Hyman, “Ze’iri interpreted”; Hyman suggests that perhaps he is Rabbi Ze’ira the reciter mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:31](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.1.1.31), folio 6b.[^6][^7]

notes.text: Saved Davidson Yoma9b names RAV PAPA, supporting ר״פ; his alternative story has Ze’iri helping ReshLakish. אלהא is an oath invoking God, followed by hostility toward the Babylonian group, not an address saying God I hate you. The two alternative pairings are not silently merged. Tanna means reciter in the final possible Ze’ira identification. All geography and generation identifications remain Hyman’s.

The consulted Yoma 9b first pairs Resh Lakish with Rabbah bar bar Chana, then objects and gives Rav Papa’s alternatives: Resh Lakish with Ze’iri, or Rabbah bar bar Chana with Elazar. Hyman selects the former alternative; the versions are not merged. The invocation is an oath followed by hostility toward the Babylonian group. Geography, relative chronology, Ze’ira identity and final reciter equation remain Hyman’s qualified reconstructions.

[Heilprin’s entry on Ze’iri](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1159&lang=en) quotes Yuchasin’s claim that Ze’iri learned from Rav and questions it. The Rosh does explicitly call Rav his teacher. In the Yevamot passage, Ze’iri adds a case to Rav’s list.

In [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.2.22), the opening attribution lists Ze’ura and Rav Chiyya bar Ashi before “in the name of Kahana.” The other three linked Yerushalmi passages name Ze’ira or Ze’ura in the name of Rabbi Chanina. Hyman’s identification with the Babylonian Ze’iri is his reading of these notices.

The text at [Chullin 56a:5-6](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.56a.5-6) has Ze’iri go up to Nehardea. [Rashi on Chullin 56a:6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.56a.6.1) adds “from Babylonia.” The contrast between “those above” and “those below” is at [Taanit 10a:14-15](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.10a.14-15). [Heilprin’s entry on Shmuel](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3336&lang=en) quotes Yuchasin’s account of the Arukh’s explanation, which places Sura below Nehardea. The consulted text of [Bava Batra 157a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.157a.11) calls the colleague Ze’ira. Rabbah’s transmission at [Nedarim 46a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.46a.9) continues on [Nedarim 46b:1-3](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.46b.1-3), where Rav Yosef objects and then gives his own version in Ze’iri’s name.

[Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:31](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.1.1.31) calls him “Rabbi Ze’ira the reciter” and identifies him as a brother of Rav Chiyya bar Ashi and Rav Abba bar Chana. Hyman’s suggestion that this is the same Ze’iri remains tentative. The formula “Ze’iri interpreted” remains unverified at the supplied Yoma 27b locator.

[Beitzah 27b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.27b.8) explicitly says that Ze’iri explained the mishnah as referring to a sacred animal. Hyman cites Yoma 27b. The formula leaves open whether he is the reciter named in the Jerusalem Talmud.
